A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fourier Position Embedding (FoPE) work. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original C4/Gutenberg training experiments, Passkey Retrieval evaluations, component ablations and toy-model normalization results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds downstream evaluations using SmolLM-1.7B and a simulated attention-mechanism comparison.

M1.justification: FoPE retains the same Fourier-series construction, coefficient initialization and clipping of frequencies below 2π/N to zero. Equations (11)–(13) and the appendix implementation listing are unchanged apart from formatting.

E1.justification: v3 adds downstream summarization and few-shot evaluation on GovReport, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA and SAMSum. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained C4/Gutenberg perplexity and synthetic Passkey Retrieval tasks.

E2.justification: The retained experiments use the same RoPE, ALiBi, YARN and normalization-related comparators. The new downstream evaluations reuse RoPE. The new mechanism illustration uses a constructed Ground Truth signal as its target, rather than introducing another baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: v3 introduces SmolLM-1.7B fine-tuning at context length 4096, followed by evaluation in 0–4k, 4–8k and 8k+ groups. The earlier 512-to-1024 extrapolation procedure remains, renamed continual pre-training. Appendix B.3 also changes the budget associated with reported pre-training runtimes from 20B to 10B tokens, aligning with the retained main-text setting without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v3 Section 5.6 and Figure 3 add a two-dimensional, single-layer MLP simulation comparing FoPE and RoPE against frequency-matched attention signals. This supplements the retained FS/CF ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity studies and QK-normalization analyses with a focused mechanism check.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 1,000 Passkey Retrieval trials per context length and the same sampling information for activation and Gaussian-vector analyses. v3 adds no training-run replication counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 adds downstream results: for example, TREC at 8k+ scores 36.00 for RoPE versus 51.00 for FoPE, while TriviaQA at 0–4k scores 36.50 versus 33.26. Figure 3 adds the finding that FoPE better follows the constructed reference signal. The retained benchmark curves and toy-model loss table match v1.

T1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds sampling-theorem statements and a corollary supporting a low-pass interpretation of RoPE. Equation (22) also corrects the Fourier-transform kernel from a positive to a negative exponent. The central NUDFT formulation and spectral-damage derivations otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the DSP account of spectral damage and the two-part FoPE method for improving length generalization. The newly named downstream experiments support the broad applicability claim already present in v1 rather than redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4 revises the zero-frequency rationale to emphasize short- and long-term dependencies and avoidance of positional bias. v3 adds interpretations of its mechanism simulation and low-pass argument. It also removes v1's explicit qualification that applying the modeling to cache compression, model collaboration and semantic communication requires further work.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 documents the new fine-tuning recipe: approximately 350k samples, one epoch, AdamW, learning rate 3e-4, cosine scheduling, 0.1 warmup ratio and four hours of training. Section 5.5 newly specifies the retained ablations' 5B-token Gutenberg setting. The repository pointer, pseudocode, hardware and original model hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Barbero et al.'s RoPE analysis, HOPE and SMR, alongside citations supporting the new model and benchmarks. The positioning that earlier approaches primarily address attention while FoPE considers other LM components remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Related work moves to Appendix A, implementation explanations move to Appendix C, and experimental settings are regrouped in Appendix B.3. The earlier fine-tuning section becomes continual pre-training, while Limitations is replaced by an Impact Statement. Prose revisions are localized; most of the existing narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the mechanism plot and downstream-results table, redraws and reorders the Q/K heatmaps, expands several captions and moves the attention-decay plot into the appendix. ICML formatting and full-width appendix text and equations substantially revise the presentation beyond simple renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1's broad length-generalization claims relied mainly on perplexity and synthetic retrieval. v3 Section 5.4 and Table 1 address an important practical-validation gap by testing instruction-fine-tuned models on downstream tasks, reporting both advantages and the TriviaQA exception, with supporting training details in Appendix B.3. This substantially strengthens empirical support for applicability. The removed applicability caveat and continued absence of run-level uncertainty limit transparency, but do not outweigh that gain.
